messages.subject: Coverting gff3 file to BED file to use as annotation object
parts:
Hi, I am working on finding DMRs for the aphid data that I have.
Following the nice manual, I was able to get myDiff object, which contains the differentially methylated regions from my data.
Now the next step would be getting the information where in the genome these DMRs are located in relation to genes, promoters, etc.

As I was working on aphid genome, which is not on the UCSC database, I downloaded gff3 format file from GenBank ftp site.
Then, I uploaded it onto Galaxy to use the gff to bed converter.
When I used the converter on Galaxy, it had multiple lines that are duplicates, as well as 6-column lines like the following.

In order to resolve the format that's suitable for the MethylKit, I made a script to simply remove any 6-column lines and duplicated lines as following.

Also, I removed the "NW_" header from the first column since the file input function doesn't seem to like the underscore character.

This step allowed me to upload the converted BED file as GRanges object when I used read.transcript.features.

However, it wouldn't let me perform the downstream analysis such as "annotate.WithGenicParts", etc.

I am wondering if anyone has experiences to work with the non-popular genome with MethylKit, where you had to download your own genome annotation, or if there's any pipeline that works on this problem.

Any help/comments would be very appreciated.

Thank you so much.


Dohyup

messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] Coverting gff3 file to BED file to use as annotation object
parts:
Hi,
The bed format looks OK, and if read.transcript.features worked it should be fine. The reason next function is not working could be because of mismatches in chromosome names. Meaning the annonation have diffent chromosome naming convention compared to CpGs, but it is hard to guess what is wrong since there is not enough info in your mail.

Best
Altuna
